# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

</system-reminder>

178	#### A. Scope, ownership, the block and the hook
179	
180	**WM-1 — Six facts, one writer each.** *Rule.* Web Map & Transit owns exactly six facts: (1) the roster records (what hulls exist and what the crew has seen of each); (2) `pod_at` (where the pod is); (3) the transit machine's state and `leg_epoch`; (4) the berth state; (5) the leg and berth *data* (content files `assets/data/world/legs.json` and `mvp_world.json`, not state); (6) the published ring reads. It never writes fuel, dormancy mechanics, pose arithmetic, geometry, air, light or stimuli (it makes no `push_stimulus` call at all; the berth's one declared LOUD noise report is Interaction's, from the `berth` declaration, IA-33, IA-40, WM-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G1)*: it calls the mutators their owners publish (Graph M16 and M19 `set_section_dormant` (ASK-G1, accepted), Body BM5, BM6 and BM7 (ASK-B1, accepted), Interaction `sync_section`, Emitter E1 at build and Emitter E10 `set_dock_status` in the applies that write `pod_at` (WM-8b)) inside one atomic apply *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and every other effect is a read. It does not define the weld offer, `q` or channels (Assembly), `room_at`, `build_section` geometry or sockets (Layout), the `docked` test (Body), fuel physics, puddles, compression or dormancy mechanics (Graph), the picker, route drawing, snap-to-node or the pause panel (Chart Table), loot or the aboard loop (Boarding & Salvage), or sounds (Adaptive Audio). It calls, cites and publishes. *Cites.* KRN CR-9; IDX:33; brief scope guard. *Pillar.* P1 (no hidden Web Map & Transit stat). *Decided.* R10, guard rail 3.
181	
182	**WM-2 — One block, one hook.** *Rule.* One SIM block `web.state` *(provisional)*: `persist` true, `persist_scope` WORLD, `scope` SHARED, `repl_hint` SHARED_SUMMARY, `schema_version` 1, `supported_versions` [1], `restore_after: [layout.state, graph.state, body.state]` and **no other entry**. `controller.state` is deliberately excluded: the registry marks it as an open conflict (REG consumer note `controller.state (OQ-9 CONFLICT)`, OQ-9), and `IN_POD` is reconciled by a read in `transit.step` rather than at restore (WM-16). One step hook `transit.step` *(provisional)*, `divisor` 1, `offset` 0, `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`; both ids exist verbatim (`body.integrate` in REG `body_state_block`, `graph.propagate.failure` LSG:64), and an unknown id in `after` would fail boot (CR-3, no alias concept). The divisor is **not a knob**: leg arrival is exact only if the hook sees every tick (WM-11). Dirty keys are explicit: `WEB/<derelict_id>`, `WEB/T` (machine and berth fields), `WEB/POD` (pod fields); the 4.7 packed-array setter change means no write may rely on a setter to mark a key (SL-15 item 9). Per tick during a leg or a berth this block marks **zero** dirty keys (progress is derived from `T - t0`); Body dirties the pod's pose each tick, which is Body's cost. The block registers one `state_hash` row (records in `mvp_world.json` order, fixed field order, no dictionary iteration; KRN D.12). *Cites.* KRN CR-3, CR-8; SL-15; REG `layout_state_block`, `body_state_block` and LSG LS-1 `graph.state` (the three `restore_after` block ids). *Pillar.* P5. *Decided.* R1.

The MVP roster is read from `assets/data/world/mvp_world.json` (`{template_id, kind, world_slot}`, DA-26, DA:140). A record is plain integers and enums; no `Vector2i`, no string, no narrative field, no "reached the centre" flag, no completion flag.

201	**WM-4 — Star topology.** *Rule.* The pod travels HOME to exactly one derelict, or from that derelict to HOME. From HOME the legal targets are derelicts whose `status` is not ABSORBED or ORPHAN and that are not berthed; from a derelict the only target is HOME. There is no derelict-to-derelict edge, no free coordinate, no steering, no route building. After B is welded and ABSORBED the home dock remains the `airlock` room and the post-weld sortie is HOME to A (loaded set S4). The MVP sentence "pick a target, hop, dock, return" is the whole topology. *Cites.* IDX:33; PCI:217 ("no pod steering at MVP"). *Pillar.* P5 (the star is the shortest honest model of "deeper"). *Decided.* R14.
202	
203	**WM-5 — The pod is one persistent Layout body, never built per hop, never breathed.** *Rule.* The pod is built **once**, at `init_world`, from the `pod` template (DA-3: one room `pod_cabin`, 2 x 2 tiles, one seat cell `seat_pod_1` (72, 48) section-local px, no fixture, no module node). It is a Layout body with its own `body_id` (BDY-25) (registry: `pod_body`) whose section is **dormant always** and is parked where `pod_at` says; Web Map & Transit adds **no other body, ever, in MVP** (lint `BODY_COUNT_MVP`): zero per-hop Class A allocation, a trivial restore, and the 4 / 3 / 4 body count of MSA-41 (home + A + B + pod before the weld, 3 after it, 4 after the one cut). Under Lighting's own definition (LO-24, LO:277: a body is **live** when it is built and has at least one non-dormant section or hosts the avatar) at most **two** bodies are live in every reachable MVP state (home plus one loaded derelict, or home plus the pod while it hosts the avatar during a leg), against `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` [PLACEHOLDER] 4 (range 2-8): a **margin of 2**. The *built* count (4 before the weld, 3 after it, 4 after the one cut) would equal the cap only under a "built" reading that Lighting does not use. ASK-LT1 is ANSWERED (Lighting states the definition). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `room_at` on the pod answers `pod_cabin`, **not** NONE (BDY-29 makes NONE on a Layout body a defect-only state that CI asserts never occurs in a clean build, AC-BDY-29a). Air during a leg is Suit's hold (WM-17), not the Graph's. *Cites.* BDY-25, BDY-29; MSA-41 (MSA:333); DA-3; REG `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` [PLACEHOLDER]. *Pillar.* P1. *Decided.* R3, R4, R25.

205	**WM-6 — Pose discipline (ASK-B1 = BM7).** *Rule.* Body has no world-pose setter: pose rows start at zero and `world += vel` each tick (BDY-26), so without a setter every loaded body would sit at world (0, 0), bodies could not be separated, and `docked` could not be established. 239	**WM-11 — The leg is a script.** *Rule.* From `t0`, Body's `body.integrate` adds the pod's whole-pixel velocity to its pose once per tick, `n` times (BDY-9 puts the pose step before actors; a BM6 applied at P2 of tick `t0` is integrated at P3 of the same tick). The pod leg is **exact**: after `n` integrations the pod is at `p1 = p0 + v x n` (formula `pod_leg`, three binding bounds: velocity at most `VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` [PLACEHOLDER], exactness per axis, coordinates at most `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` [PLACEHOLDER]; registered as formula `pod_leg`, D.1). `transit.step` (P3, after `body.integrate`) evaluates one **idempotent** rule every run: *if the state is LEG and `T >= t0 + n - 1` and no `pod_arrive` for this `leg_epoch` has applied, submit SYSTEM `pod_arrive{leg_epoch}`.* It is resubmitted until it applies, because a pending SYSTEM command is dropped on restore (WM-30). The hook writes **no state** and calls **no Class A mutator** (KRN CR-9: a hook reaches another block only through a Class B mutator or a T+1 SYSTEM command). There is no steering, no hazard, no encounter, no stimulus, no random event and no random delay: the leg takes the same time every time (the web's distances do not change, and a hop never produces an unwarned harm). The leg's data (`p0`, velocity, `n`, the approach pose) is **content** in `assets/data/world/legs.json`, linted on load; the return leg is the exact time reverse of the outbound leg, so it needs no extra authored data. *Cites.* BDY-9, BDY-26; KRN CR-9; REG `VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` [PLACEHOLDER]. *Pillar.* P2, P1. *Decided.* R2, R7.
240	
241	**WM-12 — Why arrival is a command, not a hook call.** *Rule (stated so the kernel reviewer need not ask).* BM5, BM6, BM7 and the dormancy mutator are Class A (validate-then-apply). A step hook may not call them. Arrival is therefore **two SYSTEM commands applied at P2 of tick T+1** (`pod_arrive`, `pod_settle`; WM-14), and a berth phase change is a third (`berth_step`; WM-21). They carry `allowed_origins {SYSTEM}` and no actor binding, so a PLAYER attempt is `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`. The hook's only outputs are those submissions; its only inputs are reads. *Cites.* KRN CR-9 (tail, KRN:104), KRN:200. *Pillar.* P1 (one writer per fact). *Decided.* R2.
242	
243	**WM-13 — Phase-boundary commands are pose-carrying and idempotent (OR-3).** *Rule.* Every SYSTEM command at a phase boundary (`pod_arrive`, `pod_settle`, `berth_step`) applies the **absolute end pose** of the phase it closes (`BM7`) and the next velocity (`BM6`) in the same apply; the pose is derived from persisted data (the active leg's parameters, WM-3; the payload carries epochs only, C8). Consequence: the world lands on the authored path regardless of command latency or loss. The arithmetic, from locked KRN and Body text: a SYSTEM command queued at tick `S` dispatches at `S+1`; a restore sends `Dropped(RELOAD)` to every pending command and the first tick after `RUNNING` sees an empty queue. A snapshot taken after tick `S = t0 + n - 1` (the hook has already submitted `pod_arrive`) therefore restores into a world where the command is gone; `body.integrate` at `S+1` moves the pod once more (it has now integrated `n + 1` times), the hook resubmits at `S+1` and the command applies at `S+2`. Without pose-carrying the pod would stop at `p1 + v`; with it the apply sets the pose to `p1`. **The expected slip is exactly `v x (T_apply - (t0 + n))` for any apply delay** (checkpoint 2026-10-26, C8): a restore drop costs one step as above, and a kernel queue delay of a SYSTEM command (up to +8 ticks, KRN D.4) costs up to eight; both are legitimate and are logged at DEBUG as `EXPECTED_RESTORE_SLIP` (hidden by the pod-local camera and by the black hold that follows). `LEG_POSE_MISMATCH` is raised **iff the observed pod offset from `p1` differs from that value**, and the pose is forced to `p1` by BM7 either way. The same rule governs `berth_step` (the expected slip is `v_i x (T_apply - (t_phase + n_i))` for the phase it closes). **The pose is always derived from persisted parameters** (the active leg's `{n, vx, vy, p0x, p0y}` or the active berth's phases, WM-3, OQ-WM-7); the payload carries `leg_epoch` / `berth_epoch` and `phase` only, never a pose. If BM7 is refused none of the exact leg and berth rules hold (WM-6 fallback). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Boundary values are keyed to nominal ticks, so a late apply persists nothing.** `arrive_T := t0 + n`, the settle tick `arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS`, `first_boarded_T` and each `t_phase := t_phase + n_i` are the NOMINAL ticks of the schedule, never the tick at which the (possibly restore-dropped, possibly queue-delayed) SYSTEM command happened to apply. A late apply (lag `k = T_apply - nominal`: 1 after a restore on an empty queue; `a - 1` <= 7 extra ticks per submit under queue delay, and `SLIP_MAX_TICKS` 15 with one restore, D.2; each further restore at the same boundary adds up to `QUEUE_AGE_MAX` ticks) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* therefore changes only the wall tick of the work, not any persisted Web Map & Transit or Body value, and the pose it sets is the **nominal trajectory at `T_apply`** (the closing phase's end pose plus the next phase's velocity times `k`; for `pod_arrive` and the last `berth_step` the next velocity is 0, so the pose is the end pose), which makes the restored world rejoin the uninterrupted one exactly. A late apply can still show in blocks that clock on where the avatar is during the `k` lag ticks (in the restored run the avatar is still `IN_POD`; in the uninterrupted run it is already aboard the target). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* They arise **only when the `pod_settle` apply is late** (Case B: a restore that drops the pending `pod_settle`, a snapshot after tick `arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS - 1`, or a kernel queue delay on the settle submit; a snapshot that drops only `pod_arrive` leaves the settle on its nominal tick and has none, States and Transitions, D.2, AC-WM-15a/b). Three bounded accruals are the **named exclusions**, stated numerically in AC-WM-54 (b): the Graph's divisor-6 loaded clocks on the target section (at most `ceil(k / 6)` steps, until M19 takes an `as_of_tick`, ASK-G1b, OPEN), Suit's thermal load and hold counters (the `IN_POD` ambient band versus the target section's band, both running after the OQ-WM-41 ruling, at most `ceil(k / 6)` runs) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* and Sanity's level (`aboard` false versus true, at most `ceil(k / 12)` accruals of `ABOARD_EXPOSURE`). Transient differences (the Controller's `IN_POD` exit one step late, Emitter re-arming) are gone by T* + 12, `T*` being the first tick at which both runs are IDLE. *Cites.* KRN edge cases (`Dropped(RELOAD)`, the empty first queue); BDY-9, BDY-26. *Pillar.* P1. *Decided.* OR-3 (adopts the systems-designer's SD-3 over the game-designer's "defect" reading).
244	
245	**WM-14 — Arrival: `pod_arrive` then `pod_settle` (OR-1).** *Rule.* **`pod_arrive{leg_epoch}`** applies at `t0 + n`: BM7 sets the pod pose to `p1` and BM6 sets velocity 0; `transit_state := ARRIVING`; `arrive_T := t0 + n` (the NOMINAL tick, not the apply tick, WM-13); the target's `status` goes UNSEEN to SEEN if it is currently UNSEEN (it **never regresses**: a BOARDED record stays BOARDED on a return visit; "unconditionally" is against the lamp condition, not against the current status; the hull has resolved out of the dark) and, separately, `unknown_seen := true` iff the residual lamp is lit by WM-18's predicate at that tick (monotone: it is only ever set, never cleared; the target is dormant, so its stock and node state are identical at the nominal tick and at a late apply) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (never from what the camera framed, which varies with the zoom ladder; the simulation never reads presentation). The target is **still dormant** and the avatar is **still in the pod**. During `ARRIVING` the `PROJECTOR` builds the target's scene content from static Layout data plus the Graph's persisted state, under the Pipeline's `TRANSIT_HOLD` black (it may pre-build during the leg, which gives it `HOP_LEG_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] ticks; -> ADR candidate). Exactly `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] later `transit.step` submits **`pod_settle{leg_epoch}`** (condition `transit_state == ARRIVING` **and** `T >= arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS - 1` [PLACEHOLDER], the same idempotent resubmit rule; the ARRIVING conjunct makes the deferral explicit: the hook defers, never drops, until the `pod_arrive` that opens ARRIVING has applied, and lint L3b below guarantees the order) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, which applies: re-validate the arrival cell with `can_transfer` (WM-15); clear the target's dormancy through M19 with `as_of_tick := arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` (ASK-G1 accepted; the `as_of_tick` parameter is ASK-G1b, OPEN) and re-sync its Interaction subjects (ASK-I1, accepted) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; BM5 transfers the avatar from the pod to the target body at the authored `arrive_*` cell; BM7 parks the pod beside the target dock (not drawn, WM-33); `transit_state := IDLE`; `pod_at := target`; Emitter E10 `set_dock_status(the target dock section, on)` in the same apply (WM-8b) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; on the first `pod_settle` at a record `status` goes SEEN to BOARDED and `first_boarded_T := arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` (the nominal tick); notify `POD_ARRIVED` (and `DERELICT_LOADED`). Total time in the pod is `n + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] on the nominal schedule (after a restore the avatar leaves the pod body `lag` ticks later, WM-13). **"Destination ready" is state, never a call:** `web.view.destination_ready := (transit_state == IDLE)`, a pure function of the persisted machine state alone (checkpoint 2026-10-26, C2): it is false through `ARRIVING` and becomes true from the `pod_settle` apply tick, before P5 Notify, which is the tick the avatar has actually left the pod body. The `- 1` appears **only** in the hook's submit condition (`T >= arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS - 1` [PLACEHOLDER], which queues `pod_settle` for T+1) and never in `destination_ready`, so the Pipeline can never cut to the avatar while the avatar is still on the pod body. The Pipeline ends `TRANSIT_HOLD` when that holds **and** its own projector-local readiness latch holds. If the projector is late, the simulation has already settled and the avatar stands on the destination for the late frames under black; this is acceptable because the target was frozen until `pod_settle` and the fairness window `W_MIN_WARNING_S` (10 s = 600 ticks) dwarfs the worst build lag (at most a few frames: the largest single build is B's 149 tiles, one frame at `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` 256 (LY Tuning Knobs, LY:1041; not a registry entry), and building home and B together would be ceil(331 / 256) = 2), and a projector-side `ARRIVE_SCENE_LATE` diagnostic is logged. *(orchestrator ruling OR-1: this departs from the literal wording of R12 and R26 and from the game-designer's own flag "not ruling-compliant"; it amends R12 and R26 (ruled, checkpoint 2026-10-26), OQ-WM-1, and is a CONFLICT-clarification against KRN:200 and PIPE C10 (CF-KRN, CF-PIPE).)* *Cites.* KRN:200, KRN conformance ("`PRESENTATION` and `PROJECTOR` have no submit path"), KRN Open Question 1; PIPE C10, CR-10; REG `W_MIN_WARNING_S`; `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` 256 (LY Tuning Knobs, LY:1041; not a registry entry); lint `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] >= ceil(largest single-target tiles / `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` 256 (LY Tuning Knobs, LY:1041; not a registry entry)) frames + margin (checkpoint OQ-WM-1). *Pillar.* P2. *Decided.* R2 (ARRIVING), R28; OR-1.
246	
247	**WM-15 — The arrival cell and the recovery branch.** *Rule.* The arrival cell is the authored `arrive_*` cell of the target's `entry_room_key` room: `arrive_a_dock` (168, 336), `arrive_b_dock` (168, 312), `arrive_home_airlock` (552, 696), all section-local px (DA table); each is one tile clear of the docked-podcraft prop (lint `SPAWN_BLOCKED`). It is **never searched** (BDY:703-706): it is validated clear by `can_transfer` at departure (`ARRIVAL_BLOCKED`) and re-validated in `pod_settle`. Because the target is frozen during the leg, a re-check failure is a **defect**, and the deterministic recovery is: the `pod_settle` apply takes a recovery branch (it is total; a SYSTEM command that rejected would leave the machine stuck) that starts **one reversal** to the departure body at no fuel cost, with `leg_epoch += 1`, `leg_dir` reversed and `ARRIVAL_RECHECK_FAILED` logged; a second failure on the reversal places the avatar at the authored cell of the body it is arriving at with no re-check and logs `ARRIVAL_FORCED`. This bounds the machine to at most one reversal per hop (the reversed leg is marked by the persisted `leg_reversed`, so the second failure is recognisable after a restore). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **The T5 apply list (the recovery branch, in order; nothing in it can reject).** (1) **Dormancy: no M19 call.** The target stays dormant (it was dormant through the leg and ARRIVING) and the departure body's dormancy is untouched; the dormancy clear of the normal `pod_settle` (WM-14) is never reached on this branch, which is what stops the target going live with the avatar not aboard. (2) **Body:** no BM5 (the avatar stays on the pod body); BM7 sets the pod pose to the nominal trajectory of the reversed leg at the apply tick (`p1` plus the reversed velocity times the lag `k`, WM-13); BM7 re-poses the departure body to the reversed leg's authored approach pose (D.3, the exact time reverse) and every other body to its slot-relative pose (WM-6); BM6 sets the pod velocity to `-v` (whole pixels). (3) **Record:** `t0 := arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` (the NOMINAL settle tick, never the apply tick, WM-13); `leg_epoch += 1`; `leg_dir` reversed; `target_id` and `origin_id` swapped; the active leg's parameters replaced by the time reverse `{n, -vx, -vy, p1x, p1y}` (so `p1' == p0' + v' x n` still holds for `post_restore`, WM-30); `leg_reversed := 1`; `transit_state := LEG`; `pod_at` stays IN_FLIGHT; the target's `status` is **not** advanced to BOARDED and `first_boarded_T` is **not** written (the first successful `pod_settle` at a record writes them). (4) **Emitter:** no E10 call; every dock glow stays OFF through the reversed leg and the destination dock's glow turns ON at the reversed leg's own `pod_settle` (WM-8b). (5) **Notify:** `ARRIVAL_RECHECK_FAILED` logged; no `POD_ARRIVED`, no `DERELICT_LOADED`; `POD_DEPARTED` is not re-emitted. (6) **Fuel:** none, and the hop's fuel is not refunded. `destination_ready` stays false (the machine is LEG), the reversed leg restores like any leg, and a re-check failure inside the reversed leg's own `pod_settle` (`leg_reversed` 1) takes the forced placement `ARRIVAL_FORCED` instead of a second reversal. AC-WM-135 checks the list and the `web.state` validity after the reversal. **Arrival safety is geometry-only.** `ARRIVAL_BLOCKED` and the re-check test Body's `can_transfer` (the authored cell is free and inside its section) and nothing else: they say nothing about the cell's air, temperature, fire, hull breach or any other Graph hazard. A BACK leg can therefore land the crew in a depressurised or breached home dock room; that is legal (the hop removes the player from a derelict's danger, not from the home ship's, which keeps running, WM-26b), `ARRIVAL_BLOCKED` is a geometric reason and is never raised for a hazard, and the hazard the arrival meets is the one the Graph's and Attention's own tells already gave. AC-WM-120 covers a return into a depressurised dock. Two crewmates on one cell is legal (BDY-17), so a forced placement is never a crash. *Cites.* BDY-17, BDY-25, BDY:703-706; DA table; DA-3. *Pillar.* P2 (never an unwarned lethal arrival). *Decided.* R26; recovery rule from the systems-designer (SD-18).
248	
249	**WM-16 — `IN_POD` and the Controller.** *Rule.* The Controller enters `IN_POD` on `pod_hop` `Applied` at the console (PCI:191) and leaves it in the first step in which the avatar's `body_of_actor` is no longer the pod body, a pure Body read, **not** by a call from a Web Map & Transit hook. This is a clarification of PCI:192 ("arrival body transfer complete (Transit hook)"), because the Controller's block is not in `restore_after` (WM-2) and an event-driven exit could desync from the world block on restore. `transit.step` reconciles by read only: if the machine is LEG or ARRIVING the traveller's `body_of_actor` must be the pod body (`WEB_RESTORE_STATE` if not, at restore). **ASK-C1 (accepted, PCI States table)**: derive `IN_POD` from body occupancy, so that derived state cannot desync. `controller.step` runs before `transit.step` in the tick, so it sees the new occupancy one tick late, which is harmless. *Cites.* PCI:173, :191-192, :694. *Pillar.* P1. *Decided.* R28 correction; R1. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
250

### Core Rules

*Conventions.* Rules are named `WM-n`; each states a **Rule**, the documents it **Cites**, the **Pillar** it serves, and what **Decided** it (advisor ruling `R-n`, locked GDD section, or an orchestrator ruling recorded here). Criteria are written in Acceptance Criteria as `AC-WM-nn`, edge cases as `E-nn`, formulas as `D.n` (section Formulas). Names of blocks, hooks, commands, reads, events and states introduced here are **provisional until the registry merge** and are marked *(provisional)* once per rule. A contract that a neighbour wrote as an *offer* is **confirmed or corrected** in the Interactions CONFLICT rows, never copied silently. Every `[PLACEHOLDER]` value is a placeholder at every mention; the Body, Lighting and Attention placeholders this system reuses (`WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` [PLACEHOLDER], `VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` [PLACEHOLDER], `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` [PLACEHOLDER], `AMBIENT_RING_PM` [PLACEHOLDER], `B_table` [PLACEHOLDER], `R_BREATH` [PLACEHOLDER]) belong to their owners and are cited, never restated as settled.

**Orchestrator rulings recorded in this GDD** (where two specialist proposals or a ruling's wording disagreed; each is repeated in the rule it affects and forwarded in Open Questions):

| ID | Ruling | Why | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| OR-1 | **Arrival is two SYSTEM commands**: `pod_arrive` ends the leg and enters `ARRIVING`; `pod_settle`, a fixed `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] later, makes the target live, re-checks the cell, transfers the avatar and returns to `IDLE`. **Accepted (ruled, checkpoint 2026-10-26):** R12 is amended to "the arrived one goes live in `pod_settle`" and R26 to "re-validated in `pod_settle`"; liveness and the re-check move to `pod_settle`, `ARRIVING` has a fixed simulation length, and the Pipeline (not the sim) holds the plate for any projector lag. | A `PROJECTOR` has no submit path (KRN conformance), so the simulation cannot wait for a scene-ready report; a frame-rate-dependent exit from `ARRIVING` would break replay and restore determinism; and it gives every state R2 names a job. Nothing live runs while the player is behind the black hold (P2 fairness). | WM-14 |
| OR-2 | `loaded` and `berthed` are **derived, not persisted**. `loaded(d)` reads the Graph through the pure read `section(section_id) -> {kind, dormant}` (ASK-G1, accepted: LS-19 publishes `section()`); the DIAGNOSTIC mirror of the first draft is retired (checkpoint 2026-10-26, C3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. | Two writers of one fact is a recorded failure class; SL-15 forbids clamping on restore, so a persisted mirror could only reject the whole save. | WM-3 |
| OR-3 | Phase-boundary commands are **pose-carrying** (absolute end pose, derived from persisted parameters, plus the next velocity in one apply); a pose offset of exactly `v x (T_apply - (t0 + n))` (a restore drop, or a kernel queue delay of up to +8 ticks, KRN D.4) is *expected*, not a defect; `LEG_POSE_MISMATCH` is raised iff the observed offset differs from that value (checkpoint 2026-10-26, C8). | KRN drops every pending command on restore (`Dropped(RELOAD)`); geometry must not depend on tick counting. | WM-13 |
| OR-4 | The lamp predicate is the **chain predicate** (ruled, checkpoint 2026-10-26; amends R6): **lit iff `read_view.node(fx_res).state in {OK, DEGRADED}` and `read_view.node(battery).stock > 0`** (registry: `residual_lamp_predicate`) (LS-10 states, LS-19 `node()` fields). It equals `stock > 0` in default MVP play. | R6 amended: a salvaged or destroyed lamp (M6) with a charged battery would otherwise leave a phantom light, a P1 lie by commission; DA:452's "honest reading" stands. | WM-18, OQ-WM-3 |
| OR-5 | Items **not in the original rulings**, all accepted (ruled, checkpoint 2026-10-26): the `ORPHAN` status, the `unberth` verb, the `UNBERTHED` event, the `TARGET_ABSORBED` reason, persisting the active leg's parameters (not only its id) and the active berth's path parameters. | Each closes a hole the rulings leave open (a named cut piece, the berthed-but-never-welded soft lock, a distinct diagnostic, golden saves surviving a tuning pass). | WM-3, WM-9, WM-22, WM-23, WM-30 |
| OR-6 | The fuel payer is found by **section `kind` HOME**, not by "the home body" and not by name. | After a weld, B's tank sits in the home body but B's section stays `kind` DERELICT; section kind is unambiguous. A refinement of R10. | WM-20 |
| OR-7 *(proposed, not adopted; design review 2026-10-27)* | The fuel payer is every FUEL_TANK **connected to the home fuel loop**, not only HOME-kind tanks. | The economy-designer finding: after a weld the player sees fuel they can never use to leave, and welding a fueled derelict gains them nothing. Needs a Graph read of fuel-loop connectivity that the Graph does not publish, and reopens the single-tank reserve marks, so OR-6 stands. | E-06, OQ-WM-23 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| OR-8 *(design review 2026-10-27)* | **Boundary values are keyed to nominal ticks**: `arrive_T = t0 + n`, the settle tick, `first_boarded_T` and `t_phase += n_i`; a late apply sets the nominal trajectory at the apply tick. | A restore drops pending SYSTEM commands, so a boundary applies one tick late; keying persisted values to the apply tick made the restored and uninterrupted hashes diverge forever and the restore-equivalence AC unreachable. | WM-13, WM-14, WM-21, D.2, E-23, AC-WM-54 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

#### A. Scope, ownership, the block and the hook

**WM-1 — Six facts, one writer each.** *Rule.* Web Map & Transit owns exactly six facts: (1) the roster records (what hulls exist and what the crew has seen of each); (2) `pod_at` (where the pod is); (3) the transit machine's state and `leg_epoch`; (4) the berth state; (5) the leg and berth *data* (content files `assets/data/world/legs.json` and `mvp_world.json`, not state); (6) the published ring reads. It never writes fuel, dormancy mechanics, pose arithmetic, geometry, air, light or stimuli (it makes no `push_stimulus` call at all; the berth's one declared LOUD noise report is Interaction's, from the `berth` declaration, IA-33, IA-40, WM-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G1)*: it calls the mutators their owners publish (Graph M16 and M19 `set_section_dormant` (ASK-G1, accepted), Body BM5, BM6 and BM7 (ASK-B1, accepted), Interaction `sync_section`, Emitter E1 at build and Emitter E10 `set_dock_status` in the applies that write `pod_at` (WM-8b)) inside one atomic apply *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and every other effect is a read. It does not define the weld offer, `q` or channels (Assembly), `room_at`, `build_section` geometry or sockets (Layout), the `docked` test (Body), fuel physics, puddles, compression or dormancy mechanics (Graph), the picker, route drawing, snap-to-node or the pause panel (Chart Table), loot or the aboard loop (Boarding & Salvage), or sounds (Adaptive Audio). It calls, cites and publishes. *Cites.* KRN CR-9; IDX:33; brief scope guard. *Pillar.* P1 (no hidden Web Map & Transit stat). *Decided.* R10, guard rail 3.

**WM-2 — One block, one hook.** *Rule.* One SIM block `web.state` *(provisional)*: `persist` true, `persist_scope` WORLD, `scope` SHARED, `repl_hint` SHARED_SUMMARY, `schema_version` 1, `supported_versions` [1], `restore_after: [layout.state, graph.state, body.state]` and **no other entry**. `controller.state` is deliberately excluded: the registry marks it as an open conflict (REG consumer note `controller.state (OQ-9 CONFLICT)`, OQ-9), and `IN_POD` is reconciled by a read in `transit.step` rather than at restore (WM-16). One step hook `transit.step` *(provisional)*, `divisor` 1, `offset` 0, `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`; both ids exist verbatim (`body.integrate` in REG `body_state_block`, `graph.propagate.failure` LSG:64), and an unknown id in `after` would fail boot (CR-3, no alias concept). The divisor is **not a knob**: leg arrival is exact only if the hook sees every tick (WM-11). Dirty keys are explicit: `WEB/<derelict_id>`, `WEB/T` (machine and berth fields), `WEB/POD` (pod fields); the 4.7 packed-array setter change means no write may rely on a setter to mark a key (SL-15 item 9). Per tick during a leg or a berth this block marks **zero** dirty keys (progress is derived from `T - t0`); Body dirties the pod's pose each tick, which is Body's cost. The block registers one `state_hash` row (records in `mvp_world.json` order, fixed field order, no dictionary iteration; KRN D.12). *Cites.* KRN CR-3, CR-8; SL-15; REG `layout_state_block`, `body_state_block` and LSG LS-1 `graph.state` (the three `restore_after` block ids). *Pillar.* P5. *Decided.* R1.

**WM-3 — The roster and the record.** *Rule.* The block holds one **record** per hop-addressable hull of content: HOME, A, B (the pod has no record; it is WM-5). The MVP roster is read from `assets/data/world/mvp_world.json` (`{template_id, kind, world_slot}`, DA-26, DA:140). A record is plain integers and enums; no `Vector2i`, no string, no narrative field, no "reached the centre" flag, no completion flag.

| Field | Type | Range | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `derelict_id` | i32 | stable content id | the string key is resolved to the id at load |
| `template_id` | i32 | index into the content table | `home_ship`, `derelict_a`, `derelict_b` |
| `kind` | u8 | HOME, DERELICT | fixed by the roster |

The block is small by construction (about 700 canonical bytes with field tags; budget in D.11) and comfortably inside `repl_hint` SHARED_SUMMARY; one golden save per version covers the three records and the pod. *Cites.* DA-26; SL-15; KRN D.12. *Pillar.* P5, P1. *Decided.* R1, R19, R20; OR-2.

**WM-4 — Star topology.** *Rule.* The pod travels HOME to exactly one derelict, or from that derelict to HOME. From HOME the legal targets are derelicts whose `status` is not ABSORBED or ORPHAN and that are not berthed; from a derelict the only target is HOME. There is no derelict-to-derelict edge, no free coordinate, no steering, no route building. After B is welded and ABSORBED the home dock remains the `airlock` room and the post-weld sortie is HOME to A (loaded set S4). The MVP sentence "pick a target, hop, dock, return" is the whole topology. *Cites.* IDX:33; PCI:217 ("no pod steering at MVP"). *Pillar.* P5 (the star is the shortest honest model of "deeper"). *Decided.* R14.

**WM-5 — The pod is one persistent Layout body, never built per hop, never breathed.** *Rule.* The pod is built **once**, at `init_world`, from the `pod` template (DA-3: one room `pod_cabin`, 2 x 2 tiles, one seat cell `seat_pod_1` (72, 48) section-local px, no fixture, no module node). It is a Layout body with its own `body_id` (BDY-25) (registry: `pod_body`) whose section is **dormant always** and is parked where `pod_at` says; Web Map & Transit adds **no other body, ever, in MVP** (lint `BODY_COUNT_MVP`): zero per-hop Class A allocation, a trivial restore, and the 4 / 3 / 4 body count of MSA-41 (home + A + B + pod before the weld, 3 after it, 4 after the one cut). Under Lighting's own definition (LO-24, LO:277: a body is **live** when it is built and has at least one non-dormant section or hosts the avatar) at most **two** bodies are live in every reachable MVP state (home plus one loaded derelict, or home plus the pod while it hosts the avatar during a leg), against `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` [PLACEHOLDER] 4 (range 2-8): a **margin of 2**. The *built* count (4 before the weld, 3 after it, 4 after the one cut) would equal the cap only under a "built" reading that Lighting does not use. ASK-LT1 is ANSWERED (Lighting states the definition). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `room_at` on the pod answers `pod_cabin`, **not** NONE (BDY-29 makes NONE on a Layout body a defect-only state that CI asserts never occurs in a clean build, AC-BDY-29a). Air during a leg is Suit's hold (WM-17), not the Graph's. *Cites.* BDY-25, BDY-29; MSA-41 (MSA:333); DA-3; REG `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` [PLACEHOLDER]. *Pillar.* P1. *Decided.* R3, R4, R25.

**WM-6 — Pose discipline (ASK-B1 = BM7).** *Rule.* Body has no world-pose setter: pose rows start at zero and `world += vel` each tick (BDY-26), so without a setter every loaded body would sit at world (0, 0), bodies could not be separated, and `docked` could not be established. Web Map & Transit therefore asks Body for **BM7 `set_body_pose(body_id, world_x, world_y)`**, Class A, whose `can_set_pose` rejects `|coord|` above `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` [PLACEHOLDER] *(BM7 now published by Body, BDY-21; ASK-B1; fills the slot Body's own Open Question 23 invited, BDY:1242, and subsumes re-origin, so no separate `rebase_world` exists)*. Poses are set only inside these applies, each one atomic: `init_world` (each body in its own `world_slot`, so no two bodies ever overlay); the departure apply (re-origin of the departure body, and **every body outside the leg re-posed to `init_pose(its slot) - init_pose(the departure slot)`**, so a dormant derelict is never left at an old approach pose and slot separation holds at every departure, not only at `init_world`, D.14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; `pod_arrive` (the pod forced to `p1`, WM-13); `pod_settle` (the pod parked at the target, or the T5 reversal); the `berth` and `unberth` applies; and every `berth_step` (pose-carrying, WM-13). The re-origins (`init_world`, departure, berth start) happen under black or outside the visible field; the boundary re-poses differ from the integrated pose only by the expected slip. A re-origin is a pure translation of every body with live content by one common vector, so no relative offset between bodies that share a view changes (lint `REORIGIN_IS_TRANSLATION`). Poses of dormant bodies are never read by the simulation; the PROJECTOR reads them for the exterior silhouettes at both ends of a leg (WM-18, CF-AD-3). Leg and berth coordinates stay far inside `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` [PLACEHOLDER] by construction; float32 canvas-offset exactness is `[UNV]` pending spike S2 (REG `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT`), so a failure there is cosmetic (exterior only) and never a simulation fault. **Fallback if Body refuses BM7:** the `PROJECTOR` builds exterior content only for the avatar's body and bodies `docked` to it (a presentation rule, no simulation change); `berth` becomes impossible and the design falls back to the derelict being pre-berthed at its world slot (losing "the wreck resolving out of the dark" for B only and making the leg to B a lie about distance, which is why BM7 is the recommended path). *Cites.* BDY-26, BDY-27, BDY:339; REG `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` [PLACEHOLDER]. *Pillar.* P1. *Decided.* R8. *Gcd note.* The two authored sockets differ by `frame_shift_px` (696, 384), whose gcd is 24; no equal-tick constant-velocity phase with a speed bound of `VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` [PLACEHOLDER] can reach that offset from a separated start, which is what forces BM7 rather than a clever path (derivation in Formulas).

**WM-7 — `init_world(world_seed)`.** *Rule.* Web Map & Transit owns `init_world` (kernel amendment K-2, accepted in KRN CR-18; SL-18 names it, DA:681 and BDY:339 repeat it). It runs in `LOADING` under one `WriteScope`, in `restore_after` order, with this fixed order (lint `INIT_WORLD_ORDER`): (1) Layout LM1 `build_section(template_id, kind)` x4 in `mvp_world.json` order (`home_ship`, `derelict_a`, `derelict_b`, `pod`; Graph M1 `instantiate_section` runs inside LM1, LY-25); (2) Emitter E1 for each section; (3) Interaction `place_loose` then `sync_section(home)`; (4) Body BM1 `place_actor(avatar, home body, spawn_cryo_1)` with `spawn_cryo_1` (216, 168) section-local px; (5) BM7 poses (WM-6); (6) M19 dormancy for A, B and the pod (ASK-G1, accepted; each flip is gated by the WM-24 rules, and no avatar is in A, B or the pod at this point) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; (7) Emitter E10 `set_dock_status(home dock section, on)` (the home dock's glow ON, every other dock glow stays OFF as E1 created them; WM-8b) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, then the block's records (HOME `status` BOARDED with `first_boarded_T` 0 because the crew wakes in it; A and B UNSEEN; `pod_at` HOME; `transit_state` IDLE). Any rejected call fails the whole build with `SL_NEW_GAME_NO_BASELINE`. `world_seed` is passed through and unused at MVP. Nothing is ever built after `init_world` (WM-24). *Cites.* SL-18 (SL:255), DA-26, AC-DA-98, BDY:339, LY-25. *Pillar.* P5 (the roster is never destroyed). *Decided.* R21.

#### B. The hop

**WM-8 — The pick and the console.** *Rule.* The **pick** is host-local presentation state of the Chart Table (undesigned): never simulation, never persisted, never assuming pause (KRN CR-16, KRN Open Question 6, PCI:78; pause is single-player only). The only simulation write is the PLAYER-origin command **`pod_hop{target_id}`** *(command vocabulary already lists `pod_hop`, KRN:85)* submitted by pressing the **pod console**: one of two Interaction CONSOLE subjects (`kind_hint` CONSOLE) distinguished by Layout's `console_role` (ASK-CT-13, ANSWERED 2026-10-28): the **POD** console (`pod_hop`, carry-admitted) anchored on the docked-podcraft prop in every dock room where the pod is parked, and the **DOCK** console (`berth`, `unberth`) anchored on the home airlock's prop only (WM-21: `berth` starts only from HOME); Interaction's object classes are POD_CONSOLE and DOCK_CONSOLE (IA-40); both `tool_required` NONE, each subject's `eligible` = this system's pure `console_ready(role)` predicate (`pod_at` equals this dock's record, machine `IDLE`, console in reach; and lit, for all three verbs: the `pod_hop` exemption (ASK-I2) stays REFUSED by Interaction, IA-6 and Interaction Open Question 31, and is not needed, because the console is lit by the docked pod's self-powered status glow (WM-8b), which counts as an ordinary lit fixture; `NOT_LIT` is therefore a backstop reason that is unreachable by construction at a pod console and the BS-19 invariant holds; user ruling, OQ-WM-39) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. For the DOCK subject `console_ready` additionally requires the dock to be HOME's. Within the DOCK subject the rows are selected by one more pure read published here, `berthed_present()` (true iff a derelict is berthed, from the persisted berth fields): `unberth` (priority 1, eligible iff `berthed_present`) and `berth` (priority 2, eligible iff not `berthed_present`), so Interaction's `select_verb` (IA-5) stays a function of (class, tool, eligible) and the plate shows `unberth` while a record is berthed (CT-10 R5). A DOCK press away from HOME cannot occur (no DOCK subject exists at a derelict dock, CT-10 R1b); through a test double it returns `NOT_DOCKED_HERE`. A POD press at HOME with a derelict berthed and no valid pick is routed to this system and returns `BERTH_PENDING` (WM-9, CT-10 R6). From a derelict the press carries HOME implicitly. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* The prompt belongs to Interaction; no Web Map & Transit HUD element exists (guard rail 1). The Chart Table's confirm gesture may issue a resume then the console press; that is the Chart Table's design call (Chart Table designed). **Gap carried to Authoring/Layout:** Derelict Authoring authors the docked-podcraft prop (DA-6, kit gap K-3) but no pod-console declaration; the console is this GDD's requirement on the prop's `subject_anchors` entry (ASK-L3 to Authoring and Layout, OPEN, OQ-DA-39; ASK-I1 to Interaction, accepted). *Cites.* IA:131 (`pod_hop`, "Web Map's"), IA-37; DA-6; KRN CR-16; CT-10 R1b, R6; ASK-CT-13, ASK-CT-14 (ANSWERED 2026-10-28: Interaction draws the text-free pick echo, IA-40; this system holds no pick). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* *Pillar.* P1 (the press is the commitment; the chart is a human instrument). *Decided.* R15.

**WM-8b — The docked pod lights its own console (user ruling, OQ-WM-39; closes the BS-19 dark-dock strand).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Rule.* Interaction's IA-6 stands unchanged ("No fourth exception for the pod console"; the `pod_hop` lit exemption ASK-I2 stays refused, so the Controller's `in_reach` lit conjunct is untouched). Instead **the docked-podcraft prop in every dock room carries a small self-powered status glow**: a nodeless (`node_ref` 0) FIXTURE of a new self-powered fixture class (Emitter State has since amended EM-3 and EM-11 to admit it: FIXTURE subkind DOCK_STATUS, self-powered, `node_ref` 0, one per dock room, created OFF by E1 and switched only by the SYSTEM mutator E10 `set_dock_status`; `set_switch` of either origin is rejected `NOT_SWITCHABLE` for it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G1)* that counts as an **ordinary lit fixture** for the console subject's `lit(o)` test. It is therefore **not** a fourth `act_gate` exception and Interaction changes nothing. (1) **On iff the prop is present (WM-33)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G1)*: each dock room's one DOCK_STATUS glow record is created OFF at `init_world` (Emitter E1) and this system switches it with Emitter's E10 `set_dock_status(section_id, on)` **inside the apply that writes `pod_at`**: ON for the home dock in `init_world` step 7, OFF for the origin dock in the `pod_hop` departure apply (WM-10), ON for the target dock in `pod_settle` (WM-14; this includes the settle that ends a T5 reversed leg, WM-15), and **no call at `berth` or `unberth`** (the pod does not move, `pod_at` is unwritten, and the verbs run only at HOME where the home glow is already ON). After every apply `switch_on(glow(d)) == (pod_at == record(d))`, and the glow is OFF at every dock while the pod is IN_FLIGHT, so wherever a console can be pressed the glow is ON. The Emitter call is infallible in a validated apply (an unknown or glow-less section is a lint-prevented defect, Emitter E10), so it adds no rejection path. It draws from no Graph node, no battery and no chest-lamp cell, so it is lit with the dock room unpowered, the cell spent and no glowstick in the pack or thrown (the BS-19 strand cell, AC-WM-128). (2) **Every dock room places it**, the home airlock included (Derelict Authoring DA-46 placement rule; lints `DOCK_GLOW_LIT_AT_CONSOLE` and `DOCK_GLOW_ARRIVAL_DARK`, AC-WM-127a). Every CONSOLE anchor in the room is lit by it: the POD anchor in every dock room and, at the home airlock, the DOCK anchor (WM-8); `pod_hop`, `berth` and `unberth` are therefore all lit-gated by the one glow. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (3) **It lights the console subject only:** Emitter State's falloff (`DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM`, `DOCK_STATUS_REACH_PX`; Emitter owns the peak, reach and falloff, this GDD owns none) lights the console anchor with margin, and the lint G2 of D.15 (Authoring's `DOCK_GLOW_ARRIVAL_DARK`) keeps the authored arrival cell below `LIT_OFF_PM`, so a dark derelict stays dark (darkness-first holds; the pod is the crew's one thread home) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G1)*. (4) `NOT_LIT` stays in the reason set as a backstop (a malformed prop or a test double) and is **unreachable by construction at a pod console**. (5) **BS-19 is owned jointly:** this system guarantees the switch-on calls (the E10 call sites above, AC-WM-127b) and Emitter State owns the glow record and its numbers (EM-11, D.1b, I-DOCK); Derelict Authoring lints its placement (DA-46: `DOCK_GLOW_LIT_AT_CONSOLE` = G1, `DOCK_GLOW_ARRIVAL_DARK` = G2); Boarding's AC-BS-92 strand cell passes through AC-WM-128. (6) **Presentation separation:** the art-director keeps the glow's luminance separate from the visible-unknown residual lamp's band and the glow is not Tungsten (steady Tungsten is the residual lamp's, WM-18); the glow never enters WM-18's predicate and never sets `unknown_seen`. (7) The glow is a real emitter that counts as light and is never a tell carrier (Attention AT-20 and its `g_dock` term, bounded by `DOCK_GLOW_TERM_MAX`; Emitter EM-11); this system pushes no stimulus for it (WM-26). Attention's and Emitter's text calls the pod 'berthed' where it means docked at its dock room: it has nothing to do with this system's `berth` verb (CF-EM-2). *Cites.* IA-6; EM-3, EM-11, EM-13, EM:660; BS-19, AC-BS-92; DA-6, DA-23. *Pillar.* P5 (the escape verb is never lost to the dark), P4 darkness-first. *Decided.* user ruling 2026-10-27 (design-review decision D58, cross-cutting ruling X2); it reverses this GDD's own answer to ASK-BS-W2 (no console self-light) and accepts the previously declined ASK-BS-W3 (OQ-WM-38 (a)).

the `berth` and `unberth` orders are unchanged) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, `FUEL_LOW` (WM-20; HOME-origin only), `ARRIVAL_BLOCKED` (the authored arrival cell fails Body's `can_transfer`, WM-15), `CAPACITY` (a hard runtime cap owned by another system would be exceeded by loading the target, via a pure preview; none is reachable at MVP, and the Interaction fixture budget is a lint on registered neighbourhoods, not a cap: S4's 145 subjects are an INFO upper bound with every registered neighbourhood at or under 120, so there is no overrun, D.9, E-44, OQ-WM-27) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the ordered-refusal tests AC-WM-10 and AC-WM-39 exercise it only through a capacity test double) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, `POD_NOT_READY` (**reserved, never returned at MVP**: Onboarding's later repair gate). `berth` adds `NOT_BOARDED` (any target that is not a BOARDED DERELICT: the wrong kind, UNSEEN, SEEN, ABSORBED, ORPHAN or an unknown id), `NO_MATE_SOCKET`, `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, `ALREADY_BERTHED`, validated in the total order `BUSY`, `IN_TRANSIT`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NOT_LIT`, `NOT_DOCKED_HERE`, `NOT_BOARDED`, `NO_MATE_SOCKET`, `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, `ALREADY_BERTHED`, `FUEL_LOW`, `CAPACITY` (`NO_MATE_SOCKET` before `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, both from the one `can_attach` preview; OQ-WM-19 closed) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and shares `BUSY`, `IN_TRANSIT`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NOT_LIT`, `NOT_DOCKED_HERE`, `FUEL_LOW`, `CAPACITY`. `unberth` (ruled, checkpoint 2026-10-26) shares `BUSY`, `IN_TRANSIT`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NOT_LIT`, `NOT_DOCKED_HERE` and adds `NOT_BERTHED` and `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`; it has **no `FUEL_LOW` path and no fuel floor** (never strand: a floor on `unberth` would bring back the soft lock it exists to remove), its status effects never regress B (B stays BOARDED) and `UNBERTHED` is emitted unconditionally. The restore reasons are `WEB_RESTORE_VERSION`, `WEB_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_RECORD`, `WEB_RESTORE_EPOCH`, `WEB_RESTORE_POD_BODY`, `WEB_RESTORE_STATE`, `WEB_RESTORE_LEG_INEXACT`, `WEB_RESTORE_BERTH_INEXACT`, `WEB_RESTORE_LOADED_SET` (a live derelict where the persisted machine allows none, E-29) (WM-30) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The dormancy-guard defect reasons are `WEB_DORMANCY_HOME` and `WEB_DORMANCY_AVATAR` (WM-24). A SYSTEM command whose `leg_epoch` or `berth_epoch` is stale or whose state does not match is **not** a fault: it is rejected `STALE_EPOCH` / `NOT_IN_LEG` / `NOT_ARRIVING` and counted at DEBUG (`transit_stale_cmds`), never `FAULTED` (a resubmitted command whose twin already applied is expected). The refusal reasons are **truth-only** surfaces (ASK-F1, Player Fantasy). *Cites.* KRN CR-5, CR-7; IA:131. *Pillar.* P1, P4. *Decided.* R15; OR-5.

**WM-10 — The departure apply (`pod_hop`).** *Rule.* After validation, one atomic apply in the kernel's fixed order Graph, then Layout, then Body (KRN:197; no rollback, so everything fallible is in `validate` or is a Class B clamp):
1. **Graph.** `granted := M16 withdraw_store(fuel tank, HOP_FUEL_ML)` [PLACEHOLDER] iff the origin is HOME, else nothing (WM-20). If the origin is a derelict: M19 `set_section_dormant(origin, true)` (ASK-G1, accepted) sets the origin's section dormant, gated by the WM-24 validate rules (skip if already dormant, HOME-kind guard, avatar-present guard, `SEAM_ACTIVE`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **with the avatar-present guard evaluated over the origin body's occupancy excluding the issuing traveller, whom BM5 moves out in step 3 of this same apply (WM-24 (3)); a second living actor aboard still refuses the hop `WEB_DORMANCY_AVATAR`**, and Interaction `sync_section` unregisters its subjects (ASK-I1, accepted, IA-37) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. HOME is never made dormant (home keeps running while the crew is away; the Graph's clocks run whether or not the player acts).
2. **Layout.** Nothing is built, nothing is discarded (WM-24; this corrects Layout's offer, CONFLICT row CF-LY).
3. **Body.** BM5 `transfer_actor(avatar, pod body, seat_pod_1, cause POD)`; BM7 `set_body_pose` x3 plus one per remaining body (departure body re-origin, the pod at the leg's start, the target at the leg's authored approach pose, and every other body re-posed to its slot-relative pose, WM-6; at most four calls at MVP) (ASK-B1, accepted, BDY-21) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; BM6 `set_body_velocity(pod body, vx, vy)` with a whole-pixel velocity.
4. **Record.** `transit_state := LEG`, `leg_epoch += 1`, `t0 := T`, `target_id`, `origin_id := the record pod_at held` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `leg_dir` (OUT from HOME, BACK to HOME), the active leg's parameters, `pod_at := IN_FLIGHT`; Emitter E10 `set_dock_status(the origin dock section, off)` in this same apply (the pod has left, so the origin dock's glow goes OFF; with `pod_at` IN_FLIGHT no dock glow is ON; WM-8b) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
5. **Notify.** `POD_DEPARTED` (WM-31).
The player is now `IN_POD`: locomotion intents are applied but ignored, the avatar is not drawn, and the pod is a leg's worth of transport, not a safe room: the statuses of the hold/run table (WM-17b) keep running, and a death in the pod is the Controller's DEAD (user ruling, OQ-WM-41) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. *Cites.* KRN:197, CR-9; BDY-25; PCI:173, :191. *Pillar.* P2 (the escape verb removes the player from danger and starts none). *Decided.* R2, R10, R12.

**WM-11 — The leg is a script.** *Rule.* From `t0`, Body's `body.integrate` adds the pod's whole-pixel velocity to its pose once per tick, `n` times (BDY-9 puts the pose step before actors; a BM6 applied at P2 of tick `t0` is integrated at P3 of the same tick). The pod leg is **exact**: after `n` integrations the pod is at `p1 = p0 + v x n` (formula `pod_leg`, three binding bounds: velocity at most `VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` [PLACEHOLDER], exactness per axis, coordinates at most `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` [PLACEHOLDER]; registered as formula `pod_leg`, D.1). `transit.step` (P3, after `body.integrate`) evaluates one **idempotent** rule every run: *if the state is LEG and `T >= t0 + n - 1` and no `pod_arrive` for this `leg_epoch` has applied, submit SYSTEM `pod_arrive{leg_epoch}`.* It is resubmitted until it applies, because a pending SYSTEM command is dropped on restore (WM-30). The hook writes **no state** and calls **no Class A mutator** (KRN CR-9: a hook reaches another block only through a Class B mutator or a T+1 SYSTEM command). There is no steering, no hazard, no encounter, no stimulus, no random event and no random delay: the leg takes the same time every time (the web's distances do not change, and a hop never produces an unwarned harm). The leg's data (`p0`, velocity, `n`, the approach pose) is **content** in `assets/data/world/legs.json`, linted on load; the return leg is the exact time reverse of the outbound leg, so it needs no extra authored data. *Cites.* BDY-9, BDY-26; KRN CR-9; REG `VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` [PLACEHOLDER]. *Pillar.* P2, P1. *Decided.* R2, R7.

**WM-12 — Why arrival is a command, not a hook call.** *Rule (stated so the kernel reviewer need not ask).* BM5, BM6, BM7 and the dormancy mutator are Class A (validate-then-apply). A step hook may not call them. Arrival is therefore **two SYSTEM commands applied at P2 of tick T+1** (`pod_arrive`, `pod_settle`; WM-14), and a berth phase change is a third (`berth_step`; WM-21). They carry `allowed_origins {SYSTEM}` and no actor binding, so a PLAYER attempt is `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`. The hook's only outputs are those submissions; its only inputs are reads. *Cites.* KRN CR-9 (tail, KRN:104), KRN:200. *Pillar.* P1 (one writer per fact). *Decided.* R2.

**WM-13 — Phase-boundary commands are pose-carrying and idempotent (OR-3).** *Rule.* Every SYSTEM command at a phase boundary (`pod_arrive`, `pod_settle`, `berth_step`) applies the **absolute end pose** of the phase it closes (`BM7`) and the next velocity (`BM6`) in the same apply; the pose is derived from persisted data (the active leg's parameters, WM-3; the payload carries epochs only, C8). Consequence: the world lands on the authored path regardless of command latency or loss. The arithmetic, from locked KRN and Body text: a SYSTEM command queued at tick `S` dispatches at `S+1`; a restore sends `Dropped(RELOAD)` to every pending command and the first tick after `RUNNING` sees an empty queue. A snapshot taken after tick `S = t0 + n - 1` (the hook has already submitted `pod_arrive`) therefore restores into a world where the command is gone; `body.integrate` at `S+1` moves the pod once more (it has now integrated `n + 1` times), the hook resubmits at `S+1` and the command applies at `S+2`. Without pose-carrying the pod would stop at `p1 + v`; with it the apply sets the pose to `p1`. **The expected slip is exactly `v x (T_apply - (t0 + n))` for any apply delay** (checkpoint 2026-10-26, C8): a restore drop costs one step as above, and a kernel queue delay of a SYSTEM command (up to +8 ticks, KRN D.4) costs up to eight; both are legitimate and are logged at DEBUG as `EXPECTED_RESTORE_SLIP` (hidden by the pod-local camera and by the black hold that follows). `LEG_POSE_MISMATCH` is raised **iff the observed pod offset from `p1` differs from that value**, and the pose is forced to `p1` by BM7 either way. The same rule governs `berth_step` (the expected slip is `v_i x (T_apply - (t_phase + n_i))` for the phase it closes). **The pose is always derived from persisted parameters** (the active leg's `{n, vx, vy, p0x, p0y}` or the active berth's phases, WM-3, OQ-WM-7); the payload carries `leg_epoch` / `berth_epoch` and `phase` only, never a pose. If BM7 is refused none of the exact leg and berth rules hold (WM-6 fallback). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Boundary values are keyed to nominal ticks, so a late apply persists nothing.** `arrive_T := t0 + n`, the settle tick `arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS`, `first_boarded_T` and each `t_phase := t_phase + n_i` are the NOMINAL ticks of the schedule, never the tick at which the (possibly restore-dropped, possibly queue-delayed) SYSTEM command happened to apply. A late apply (lag `k = T_apply - nominal`: 1 after a restore on an empty queue; `a - 1` <= 7 extra ticks per submit under queue delay, and `SLIP_MAX_TICKS` 15 with one restore, D.2; each further restore at the same boundary adds up to `QUEUE_AGE_MAX` ticks) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* therefore changes only the wall tick of the work, not any persisted Web Map & Transit or Body value, and the pose it sets is the **nominal trajectory at `T_apply`** (the closing phase's end pose plus the next phase's velocity times `k`; for `pod_arrive` and the last `berth_step` the next velocity is 0, so the pose is the end pose), which makes the restored world rejoin the uninterrupted one exactly. A late apply can still show in blocks that clock on where the avatar is during the `k` lag ticks (in the restored run the avatar is still `IN_POD`; in the uninterrupted run it is already aboard the target). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* They arise **only when the `pod_settle` apply is late** (Case B: a restore that drops the pending `pod_settle`, a snapshot after tick `arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS - 1`, or a kernel queue delay on the settle submit; a snapshot that drops only `pod_arrive` leaves the settle on its nominal tick and has none, States and Transitions, D.2, AC-WM-15a/b). Three bounded accruals are the **named exclusions**, stated numerically in AC-WM-54 (b): the Graph's divisor-6 loaded clocks on the target section (at most `ceil(k / 6)` steps, until M19 takes an `as_of_tick`, ASK-G1b, OPEN), Suit's thermal load and hold counters (the `IN_POD` ambient band versus the target section's band, both running after the OQ-WM-41 ruling, at most `ceil(k / 6)` runs) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* and Sanity's level (`aboard` false versus true, at most `ceil(k / 12)` accruals of `ABOARD_EXPOSURE`). Transient differences (the Controller's `IN_POD` exit one step late, Emitter re-arming) are gone by T* + 12, `T*` being the first tick at which both runs are IDLE. *Cites.* KRN edge cases (`Dropped(RELOAD)`, the empty first queue); BDY-9, BDY-26. *Pillar.* P1. *Decided.* OR-3 (adopts the systems-designer's SD-3 over the game-designer's "defect" reading).

**WM-14 — Arrival: `pod_arrive` then `pod_settle` (OR-1).** *Rule.* **`pod_arrive{leg_epoch}`** applies at `t0 + n`: BM7 sets the pod pose to `p1` and BM6 sets velocity 0; `transit_state := ARRIVING`; `arrive_T := t0 + n` (the NOMINAL tick, not the apply tick, WM-13); the target's `status` goes UNSEEN to SEEN if it is currently UNSEEN (it **never regresses**: a BOARDED record stays BOARDED on a return visit; "unconditionally" is against the lamp condition, not against the current status; the hull has resolved out of the dark) and, separately, `unknown_seen := true` iff the residual lamp is lit by WM-18's predicate at that tick (monotone: it is only ever set, never cleared; the target is dormant, so its stock and node state are identical at the nominal tick and at a late apply) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (never from what the camera framed, which varies with the zoom ladder; the simulation never reads presentation). The target is **still dormant** and the avatar is **still in the pod**. During `ARRIVING` the `PROJECTOR` builds the target's scene content from static Layout data plus the Graph's persisted state, under the Pipeline's `TRANSIT_HOLD` black (it may pre-build during the leg, which gives it `HOP_LEG_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] ticks; -> ADR candidate). Exactly `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] later `transit.step` submits **`pod_settle{leg_epoch}`** (condition `transit_state == ARRIVING` **and** `T >= arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS - 1` [PLACEHOLDER], the same idempotent resubmit rule; the ARRIVING conjunct makes the deferral explicit: the hook defers, never drops, until the `pod_arrive` that opens ARRIVING has applied, and lint L3b below guarantees the order) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, which applies: re-validate the arrival cell with `can_transfer` (WM-15); clear the target's dormancy through M19 with `as_of_tick := arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` (ASK-G1 accepted; the `as_of_tick` parameter is ASK-G1b, OPEN) and re-sync its Interaction subjects (ASK-I1, accepted) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; BM5 transfers the avatar from the pod to the target body at the authored `arrive_*` cell; BM7 parks the pod beside the target dock (not drawn, WM-33); `transit_state := IDLE`; `pod_at := target`; Emitter E10 `set_dock_status(the target dock section, on)` in the same apply (WM-8b) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; on the first `pod_settle` at a record `status` goes SEEN to BOARDED and `first_boarded_T := arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` (the nominal tick); notify `POD_ARRIVED` (and `DERELICT_LOADED`). Total time in the pod is `n + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] on the nominal schedule (after a restore the avatar leaves the pod body `lag` ticks later, WM-13). **"Destination ready" is state, never a call:** `web.view.destination_ready := (transit_state == IDLE)`, a pure function of the persisted machine state alone (checkpoint 2026-10-26, C2): it is false through `ARRIVING` and becomes true from the `pod_settle` apply tick, before P5 Notify, which is the tick the avatar has actually left the pod body. The `- 1` appears **only** in the hook's submit condition (`T >= arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS - 1` [PLACEHOLDER], which queues `pod_settle` for T+1) and never in `destination_ready`, so the Pipeline can never cut to the avatar while the avatar is still on the pod body. The Pipeline ends `TRANSIT_HOLD` when that holds **and** its own projector-local readiness latch holds. If the projector is late, the simulation has already settled and the avatar stands on the destination for the late frames under black; this is acceptable because the target was frozen until `pod_settle` and the fairness window `W_MIN_WARNING_S` (10 s = 600 ticks) dwarfs the worst build lag (at most a few frames: the largest single build is B's 149 tiles, one frame at `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` 256 (LY Tuning Knobs, LY:1041; not a registry entry), and building home and B together would be ceil(331 / 256) = 2), and a projector-side `ARRIVE_SCENE_LATE` diagnostic is logged. *(orchestrator ruling OR-1: this departs from the literal wording of R12 and R26 and from the game-designer's own flag "not ruling-compliant"; it amends R12 and R26 (ruled, checkpoint 2026-10-26), OQ-WM-1, and is a CONFLICT-clarification against KRN:200 and PIPE C10 (CF-KRN, CF-PIPE).)* *Cites.* KRN:200, KRN conformance ("`PRESENTATION` and `PROJECTOR` have no submit path"), KRN Open Question 1; PIPE C10, CR-10; REG `W_MIN_WARNING_S`; `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` 256 (LY Tuning Knobs, LY:1041; not a registry entry); lint `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] >= ceil(largest single-target tiles / `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` 256 (LY Tuning Knobs, LY:1041; not a registry entry)) frames + margin (checkpoint OQ-WM-1). *Pillar.* P2. *Decided.* R2 (ARRIVING), R28; OR-1.

**WM-15 — The arrival cell and the recovery branch.** *Rule.* The arrival cell is the authored `arrive_*` cell of the target's `entry_room_key` room: `arrive_a_dock` (168, 336), `arrive_b_dock` (168, 312), `arrive_home_airlock` (552, 696), all section-local px (DA table); each is one tile clear of the docked-podcraft prop (lint `SPAWN_BLOCKED`). It is **never searched** (BDY:703-706): it is validated clear by `can_transfer` at departure (`ARRIVAL_BLOCKED`) and re-validated in `pod_settle`. Because the target is frozen during the leg, a re-check failure is a **defect**, and the deterministic recovery is: the `pod_settle` apply takes a recovery branch (it is total; a SYSTEM command that rejected would leave the machine stuck) that starts **one reversal** to the departure body at no fuel cost, with `leg_epoch += 1`, `leg_dir` reversed and `ARRIVAL_RECHECK_FAILED` logged; a second failure on the reversal places the avatar at the authored cell of the body it is arriving at with no re-check and logs `ARRIVAL_FORCED`. This bounds the machine to at most one reversal per hop (the reversed leg is marked by the persisted `leg_reversed`, so the second failure is recognisable after a restore). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **The T5 apply list (the recovery branch, in order; nothing in it can reject).** (1) **Dormancy: no M19 call.** The target stays dormant (it was dormant through the leg and ARRIVING) and the departure body's dormancy is untouched; the dormancy clear of the normal `pod_settle` (WM-14) is never reached on this branch, which is what stops the target going live with the avatar not aboard. (2) **Body:** no BM5 (the avatar stays on the pod body); BM7 sets the pod pose to the nominal trajectory of the reversed leg at the apply tick (`p1` plus the reversed velocity times the lag `k`, WM-13); BM7 re-poses the departure body to the reversed leg's authored approach pose (D.3, the exact time reverse) and every other body to its slot-relative pose (WM-6); BM6 sets the pod velocity to `-v` (whole pixels). (3) **Record:** `t0 := arrive_T + ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` (the NOMINAL settle tick, never the apply tick, WM-13); `leg_epoch += 1`; `leg_dir` reversed; `target_id` and `origin_id` swapped; the active leg's parameters replaced by the time reverse `{n, -vx, -vy, p1x, p1y}` (so `p1' == p0' + v' x n` still holds for `post_restore`, WM-30); `leg_reversed := 1`; `transit_state := LEG`; `pod_at` stays IN_FLIGHT; the target's `status` is **not** advanced to BOARDED and `first_boarded_T` is **not** written (the first successful `pod_settle` at a record writes them). (4) **Emitter:** no E10 call; every dock glow stays OFF through the reversed leg and the destination dock's glow turns ON at the reversed leg's own `pod_settle` (WM-8b). (5) **Notify:** `ARRIVAL_RECHECK_FAILED` logged; no `POD_ARRIVED`, no `DERELICT_LOADED`; `POD_DEPARTED` is not re-emitted. (6) **Fuel:** none, and the hop's fuel is not refunded. `destination_ready` stays false (the machine is LEG), the reversed leg restores like any leg, and a re-check failure inside the reversed leg's own `pod_settle` (`leg_reversed` 1) takes the forced placement `ARRIVAL_FORCED` instead of a second reversal. AC-WM-135 checks the list and the `web.state` validity after the reversal. **Arrival safety is geometry-only.** `ARRIVAL_BLOCKED` and the re-check test Body's `can_transfer` (the authored cell is free and inside its section) and nothing else: they say nothing about the cell's air, temperature, fire, hull breach or any other Graph hazard. A BACK leg can therefore land the crew in a depressurised or breached home dock room; that is legal (the hop removes the player from a derelict's danger, not from the home ship's, which keeps running, WM-26b), `ARRIVAL_BLOCKED` is a geometric reason and is never raised for a hazard, and the hazard the arrival meets is the one the Graph's and Attention's own tells already gave. AC-WM-120 covers a return into a depressurised dock. Two crewmates on one cell is legal (BDY-17), so a forced placement is never a crash. *Cites.* BDY-17, BDY-25, BDY:703-706; DA table; DA-3. *Pillar.* P2 (never an unwarned lethal arrival). *Decided.* R26; recovery rule from the systems-designer (SD-18).

**WM-16 — `IN_POD` and the Controller.** *Rule.* The Controller enters `IN_POD` on `pod_hop` `Applied` at the console (PCI:191) and leaves it in the first step in which the avatar's `body_of_actor` is no longer the pod body, a pure Body read, **not** by a call from a Web Map & Transit hook. This is a clarification of PCI:192 ("arrival body transfer complete (Transit hook)"), because the Controller's block is not in `restore_after` (WM-2) and an event-driven exit could desync from the world block on restore. `transit.step` reconciles by read only: if the machine is LEG or ARRIVING the traveller's `body_of_actor` must be the pod body (`WEB_RESTORE_STATE` if not, at restore). **ASK-C1 (accepted, PCI States table)**: derive `IN_POD` from body occupancy, so that derived state cannot desync. `controller.step` runs before `transit.step` in the tick, so it sees the new occupancy one tick late, which is harmless. *Cites.* PCI:173, :191-192, :694. *Pillar.* P1. *Decided.* R28 correction; R1. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

273	**WM-20 — Fuel is the Graph's: Web Map & Transit spends, never stores.** *Rule.* A hop and a berth *spend* fuel through M16 `withdraw_store(node_id, amount) -> granted` (Class B, clamps to stock, so `apply` is total). **Who pays:** a hop pays `HOP_FUEL_ML` [PLACEHOLDER] on departure from HOME only (the round trip is prepaid; the return hop costs `RETURN_HOP_FUEL_ML` [PLACEHOLDER], a knob kept at 0), and `berth` pays its own constant `BERTH_FUEL_ML` [PLACEHOLDER]. **Where from:** the FUEL_TANK node(s) in sections whose `kind` is HOME, found by kind through the Graph's pure `section(section_id) -> {kind, dormant}` read (ASK-G1, accepted), **never by the string `ft_main`** (lint); if there is more than one payer tank, withdrawal runs in ascending node id until the cost is met (the Graph's own convention, LSG:111); a DERELICT-kind tank (for example B's `ft_b` after a weld) is never drawn on, so it is not an MVP refuel source *(OR-6, refining R10)*. **Validate:** the pool is the sum of the payer tanks' persisted stock read from `read_view.node(tank).stock`; `pod_hop` and `berth` are rejected `FUEL_LOW` when `pool - cost < HOP_FUEL_FLOOR_ML` [PLACEHOLDER] (accepted when equal). **Apply:** `granted := withdraw_store(...)`; a `granted` below the cost cannot occur on a validated command in the same tick (one command per apply, no interleaving) and, if it ever did, is logged `transit_fuel_short` and the hop **still proceeds** (never strand). The floor must not stay a hidden threshold (P1 design test: a hidden stat versus a visibly leaking pipe -> the pipe); the first draft's refusal-only witness was a P1 risk (stage 12). The berth path is **authored per derelict as a piecewise-constant-velocity path** of at most three phases with an exact-sum lint (the start offset is *derived* from the path so exactness is structural), each speed at most `VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` [PLACEHOLDER], the last phase a slow contact crawl so the `BERTHED` contact beat is soft, and a start far enough outside the visible field that no pose is seen to jump (values and lints in D.7). The player is *not* in the pod during a berth: they stand inside the home hull (the camera is avatar-local on the home body), and the interior never shows the ship's own motion, so there is no progress element and no picture; the witnesses are a sustained drive-hum and hull-strain bed across the whole of BERTHING (its audible length is the closing's length), the `BERTHED` contact cue with its Settle, and the weld offer appearing (Visual/Audio §2 and §8, Game Feel). The drive burn the player hears is the drive burn reported to Attention as one LOUD push at the apply, pushed by Interaction (WM-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G1)*. *Cites.* MSA-12 (MSA:206), MSA-25; BDY-26, BDY-27, REG `docking_invariant`; LSG LS-17; REG `mvp_template_roster` sockets. *Pillar.* P1 (the weld starts with a physical meeting, not a menu), P5 (growth costs fuel). *Decided.* R9. *Why this over the alternatives.* A derelict pre-berthed from minute 0 would make the closing a lie about the cost and the time of coming alongside (the hop to B is separately shown by its exterior leg); hiding `delta_abs` behind a camera cut shows a jump, which BDY-27 permits only where this system cannot guarantee `docked`.

283	**WM-24 — The loaded set and dormancy policy.** *Rule.* The loaded set is the HOME body (with any welded pieces) plus **at most one unwelded derelict**; the pod's section is always dormant. A departed derelict goes dormant **in the departure apply** (WM-10); the arrived derelict goes live **in `pod_settle`** (WM-14, OR-1); `berth` loads B (WM-21); a reconcile may set an orphan dormant (WM-23). **Nothing is ever built, discarded or re-instantiated on a hop**: every section is built once at `init_world`, and a hop only flips dormancy, unregisters or re-syncs Interaction subjects, and (in the `PROJECTOR`) frees or rebuilds scene content. This is a CONFLICT-clarification against Layout's offer that Web Map & Transit uses `build_section` (LM1) "for the pod hop's atomic data change" (LY:444): it is not used on a hop (CF-LY). The reachable sets are exactly the five of DA-32 (confirmed here, answering OQ-DA-15's first question): **S0** {home}; **S1** {home, A}; **S2** {home, B}; **S3** {home + B welded}; **S4** {home + B, A} (the post-weld sortie to A). Set transitions: S0 to S1 (hop to A, live at `pod_settle`); S1 to S0 (hop home, A dormant at departure); S0 to S2 (hop to B, or `berth` B); S2 to S0 (B dormant on the hop home or on `unberth`); S2 to S3 (weld); S3 to S4 (hop to A); S4 to S3 (hop home); S3 to a S0-shaped set (cut: the orphan is dormant). **During a leg the loaded set is {home}** (both derelicts dormant). `BERTH_PENDING` and the star topology (WM-4) make every set outside S0 to S4 unreachable. DA-32 budgets, quoted: subjects `S_int` 70 / 102 / 113 / 113 / 145 as INFO upper bounds (D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* against `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` [PLACEHOLDER] 120 (an Interaction lint value, not a registry entry; it applies to registered neighbourhoods, each at or under 120, so S4 is no longer an overrun, DA-47, D37, E-44, OQ-WM-27) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; world tiles 182 / 300 / 331 / 331 / 449 (453 with the pod body), against `TILES_WORLD_MVP` 600 (LY D.13; a Layout Tuning Knob, not a registry entry) with a WARN at 540. Dormancy-at-once is necessary but **not sufficient** for S4's subject count (all four S4 members are legitimately live, so this system has no lever on it); the arithmetic is in D.9. **ASK-G1 is ACCEPTED** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the Graph publishes M19 `set_section_dormant(section_id, dormant)` (Class A, LS-17, LS-18; pure check `check_set_section_dormant`) and the pure read `section(section_id) -> {kind, dormant}` (LS-19). M19's reasons are `SECTION_UNKNOWN`, `NO_CHANGE` (already in that state) and `SEAM_ACTIVE` (an ACTIVE seam joins it to a loaded section); the earlier proposed names `SECTION_HOME`, `SECTION_JOINED` and `SECTION_TOMBSTONED` are withdrawn.
